body: Monster Max is Rare's Game Boy isometric puzzle adventure about an aspiring rock star opposing King Krond's ban on music. Max enters the Mega Hero Academy, working through its floors and completing tasks that earn access to further rooms. The view makes blocks, platforms and the character's position central to understanding each problem. A small chamber can require several actions in a particular order, with movement around its objects providing the means of testing whether the apparent solution actually leaves a way to reach the next step.

Room objectives include collecting particular objects and dealing with enemies, while the academy's terminals explain the tasks ahead. The challenge depends on reading the arrangement and recognising which action needs to happen first. An object that looks easy to reach may still require another part of the room to be prepared. Gold earned through completed tasks pays for access to higher floors, linking each solved puzzle to the larger climb through the academy. The same small set of movements keeps acquiring another purpose as the rooms change.

Jon Ritman handled design and programming, Bernie Drummond created the graphics and David Wise composed the music. Ritman and Drummond brought experience from Batman and Head over Heels, applying their interest in three-dimensional-looking rooms to the Game Boy. Titus released Monster Max in Europe in 1994 after development had finished much earlier. Its scale is expressed through a long sequence of carefully arranged spaces rather than an expansive view. The player becomes familiar with the little figure by repeatedly discovering what the next room allows him to do.
